metadata.name: paste
metadata.displayName: paste - Merge lines of files side by side
metadata.description: Combine corresponding lines from files into columns

installation.note: paste is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: The paste command merges lines from one or more files by placing them side-by-side, separated by a delimiter (tab by default). It's useful for quickly creating simple tables from multiple files.
when_to_use: Combine two columns stored in separate files
Create a quick tabular view from line-based data
Prepare simple TSV/CSV-like output for further processing

syntax.description: With multiple files, paste outputs each line by taking one line from each file in order.

options.description: Use the given list of delimiters instead of tab
Paste one file at a time instead of in parallel (turns lines into a single line)
options.use_case: To convert a newline-separated list into a comma-separated list

examples.title: Combine two files into two columns
examples.description: Create a simple two-column table using tab delimiters

examples.title: Convert a list into a single comma-separated line
examples.description: Join all lines from a file into one CSV line
examples.use_case: Create a comma-separated list for scripting

related_commands.description: Join files based on a key field (not line position)
Extract columns from delimited text; often used after paste
